steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.

title: PN-Mix: Pair-Norm Guided Mixed-Precision Key Cache Quantization for Efficient Long-Output LLM Inference
summary: PN-Mix replaces fixed-precision or purely key-statistics-based mixed-precision KV cache quantization with saliency allocation driven by query-key pair-norm products at the RoPE channel-pair level, identified once during prefill and reused during decoding. The cost is a one-time prefill saliency analysis, implementation of per-channel-pair mixed-precision kernels, and residual accuracy loss at very low bit rates compared to full-precision caching. It can fail on non-RoPE or non-decoder-only architectures, on workloads whose saliency profile shifts between prefill and long decoding, and if custom kernel overhead negates the memory-bandwidth savings on a single-GPU serving stack.
rationale: The method directly targets KV cache memory and bandwidth bottlenecks in long-output inference on a single GPU with a plausible quality gain over existing low-bit baselines, but the realized benefit depends on the reader's model, output lengths, and availability of efficient mixed-precision kernels, so workload-specific validation is required before production adoption.

claims.statement: PN-Mix replaces fixed-precision or purely key-statistics-based mixed-precision KV cache quantization with saliency allocation driven by query-key pair-norm products at the RoPE channel-pair level, identified once during prefill and reused during decoding. The cost is a one-time prefill saliency analysis, implementation of per-channel-pair mixed-precision kernels, and residual accuracy loss at very low bit rates compared to full-precision caching. It can fail on non-RoPE or non-decoder-only architectures, on workloads whose saliency profile shifts between prefill and long decoding, and if custom kernel overhead negates the memory-bandwidth savings on a single-GPU serving stack.

PN-Mix at 2.26-bit average key precision matches or exceeds prior mixed-precision methods using 2.32-2.39 bits on reasoning, code-generation, and AIME benchmarks, and degrades gracefully down to 1.5 bits where baselines drop sharply below 2.25 bits.
